map.输入样地面积、平均胸径、平均树高、株数，采用实验形数法估算林木蓄积量: Enter the sample plot area, mean breast diameter, mean tree height and tree count to estimate the stand stock with the experimental form factor method
map.核心计算公式（按输入变量）：totalV÷area×10000；π×dbh×db: Core formula (by input variable): totalV÷area×10000; π×dbh×dbh÷4÷10000; mPerHa÷15
map.📖 查看「实验形数法蓄积估算使用指南」: 📖 Read the "Experimental form factor stock estimation usage guide"
map.💡 公式：单株材积 V = g × H × f，其中 g = π×D²÷4 ÷: 💡 Formula: single-tree volume V = g × H × f, where g = π×D²÷4 ÷ 10000 (m²); stock per unit area M = V × N ÷ sample plot area × 10000 (m³/ha). The experimental form factor is usually taken as 0.40-0.52.
map.实验形数 f：针叶树常取 0.45~0.50，阔叶树常取 0.40~0.45，可: Experimental form factor f: 0.45-0.50 for conifers and 0.40-0.45 for broadleaves, adjustable from the reference dropdown

map.📚 深度解析：实验形数法蓄积估算: 📚 Deep dive: Experimental Form Factor Stock Estimation
map.样地单株材积估算: Single-tree volume estimation on a sample plot
map.森林资源调查林分评估: Stand assessment in forest resource inventories
map.单株断面积 g=π·DBH²/4/10000；单株材积 v=g×树高×实验形数: Single-tree basal area g=π·DBH²/4/10000; single-tree volume v=g × tree height × experimental form factor f (conifers f≈0.45-0.50, broadleaves ≈0.40-0.45); the plot total is Σv, stock per hectare = plot total / plot area × 10000, and per mu = per hectare / 15.
map.样地 667 m²、株数 120、胸径 14 cm、树高 12 m、f=0.5：: A 667 m² plot with 120 trees, 14 cm breast diameter, 12 m height and f=0.5: g=0.0154 m², v=0.0154×12×0.5=0.0924 m³, total stock=11.08 m³, stock per hectare=11.08/667×10000≈166.2 m³/ha (≈11.1 m³/mu).
map.实验形数和二元材积表差多少？: How much do the form factor and the two-entry volume table differ?
map.实验形数法是近似，二元材积表更准；大范围调查应以当地材积表为准，形数法仅作快速估: The form factor method is an approximation while the two-entry volume table is more accurate; large-area surveys should follow the local volume table, and the form factor method serves only for quick estimates.
map.针叶树阔叶树形数取值为何不同？: Why do conifers and broadleaves use different form factors?
map.树干干形差异：针叶树通直、形数偏大，阔叶树常分杈、形数偏小，故取不同区间以提高估: Because the trunk forms differ: conifers have straight boles with a larger form factor, while broadleaves often fork and have a smaller one, so different ranges are used to improve estimation accuracy.
